claims.text: ``gate`` is the task's OWN curated command gate ({"argv", "cwd", "timeout_s"}), forwarded by the caller from the picker candidate that produced this work. ``None``/empty reproduces the previous behaviour byte-for-byte, including the effect-key digest: ``TaskSpec.body()`` admits ``gate`` into the canonical body only when ``gate_argv`` is non-empty, so no task that lacks one sees its digest move.
claims.why: The claim about TaskSpec.body() and digest is not verifiable from this chunk; no definition of body() or digest logic is present.

claims.text: WHY THIS IS NOT A NEW EXECUTION RISK. The argv is repo-authored, not model-authored: ``spine/picker.py`` builds it (docref's is ``sys.executable -m daedalus.spine.docref_gate ...``), and the work-queue source validates it as a NUL-free string array out of a repo-curated file. It is then executed by ``spine.attempt.command_gate`` as an argv list with no shell, at LOW INTEGRITY inside containment, in a Job Object, in the candidate's own worktree -- the same instrument, with the same containment, that already runs every default pytest gate. A model-written patch cannot reach this path without a human `git merge` first, because the picker reads the primary checkout and promotion stops at an integration branch.
claims.why: The claim references external modules (spine/picker.py, spine.attempt.command_gate) and containment details not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ``_relay_gate`` AND the task's own curated command gate, in that order. THIS COMPOSITION IS THE WHOLE POINT, and it exists because putting ``gate_argv`` on the TaskSpec alone would have done NOTHING: ``TaskAttempt.__init__`` gives an explicitly-passed ``gate=`` precedence over ``task.gate_argv``, and this module always passes one. A curated gate that is silently ignored is worse than none.
claims.why: The claim about TaskAttempt.__init__ precedence is not verifiable from this chunk; no definition of TaskAttempt is present.

claims.text: Order matters, and it is not arbitrary: 1. ``_relay_gate`` first, as a PRECONDITION. It is the only check that catches ``offload()`` finishing ``escalated_after_verify_fail`` with a NON-EMPTY ``wrote`` -- a write it could not fully roll back, kept visible on purpose. Those bytes are a failed run's debris; judging them with a docref re-scan could well return "references resolve" and would promote debris. Replacing the relay gate rather than preceding it would have opened exactly that hole. 2. The curated command gate second, as the DISCRIMINATOR -- the thing that actually knows whether THIS task succeeded.
claims.why: The claim references offload() and relay gate behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Both verdicts are returned UNCHANGED (never re-wrapped into a fresh GateResult), so containment attestations and gate output survive whichever one decides. Fail-closed: both must pass.
claims.why: The code in _curated_relay_gate returns the result of relay(ctx) directly if it fails, and otherwise returns the result of command_gate(...)(ctx) directly; no re-wrapping occurs. Both must pass because if first fails, the function returns early without calling command_gate.

claims.text: PHASE 1: run every write Assignment through ``TaskAttempt``, concurrently. Returns one ``GatedCandidate`` per assignment, in ``assignments`` order (not completion order). Never touches the primary checkout -- see module docstring.
claims.why: Code uses ThreadPoolExecutor to submit all assignments, collects results into a list indexed by original order, and returns that list. No checkout modification is visible in this chunk.

claims.text: ``cancel``, when given, is forwarded to every ``TaskAttempt`` unchanged -- ``daedalus.spine.attempt._as_predicate`` normalises it (a bare callable, or anything exposing ``is_set()``, both work with no adapter here). ``None`` (the default) reproduces today's behaviour exactly: no attempt in this batch is cooperatively cancellable. This is deliberately request-scoped, not a module-level killswitch lookup -- a caller (e.g. a loop driver) that wants every attempt in one batch to share one cancel token passes it once, here; this module does not reach for global cancellation state on its own.
claims.why: The claim about _as_predicate normalisation is not verifiable from this chunk; no definition of that function is present. The code does forward cancel unchanged to _attempt_assignment, which passes it to run_attempt.

claims.text: ``artifact_dir`` is optional for direct callers. ``run_write_wave`` always supplies the checkout-external content-addressed archive because it returns dictionaries rather than the live ``GatedCandidate`` objects.
claims.why: The claim about run_write_wave is not verifiable from this chunk; that function is not present.

claims.text: Same primitives as ``daedalus.budget._BudgetLock`` and ``runs/council/room.py``'s ``_RoomLock`` (``msvcrt`` on Windows, ``fcntl`` on POSIX), independently written here -- both of those are private to modules this file does not own. Same fail-closed posture as the budget lock, and for the same reason: two promotions racing into one integration worktree is exactly the shared-mutable-state hazard this whole module exists to close, just moved one layer up. An unobtainable lock RAISES; it never silently proceeds unserialised.
claims.why: The code uses msvcrt on Windows and fcntl on POSIX for locking. It raises PromotionUnavailable when the lock cannot be acquired within timeout, and never silently proceeds. The retry loop and exception handling match the claim.

claims.text: Resolve model assignments against the PRIMARY checkout. The isolated worktree is cut from committed HEAD and therefore (correctly) excludes dirty policy edits; letting offload rediscover the assignment there silently changed Lucia's measured 14B run back to the .env default.
claims.why: The claim about offload rediscovery and Lucia's run is not verifiable from this chunk; no definition of offload or Lucia is present.

observations.what: _curated_relay_gate returns a closure that calls _relay_gate and command_gate; both must pass.
gate_candidates uses ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers=max(1, max_workers); max_workers=0 would become 1.
_PromotionLock.__enter__ retries locking in a loop with 0.2s sleep; if all attempts fail, it closes the file handle and raises PromotionUnavailable.
_PromotionLock.__exit__ unlocks using the same platform-specific primitives; if _fh is None, it returns False immediately.

risks: _curated_relay_gate | low | Returns a closure that calls _relay_gate and command_gate; both must pass. | Review that _relay_gate and command_gate are correctly defined and imported.

gate_candidates | low | Uses ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers=max(1, max_workers); if max_workers=0, it becomes 1. | Confirm that the caller never passes 0 or negative; if so, document the clamping.
_PromotionLock.__enter__ | low | Retries locking with 0.2s sleep; if all attempts fail, closes file handle and raises. | Ensure no other code holds the lock indefinitely; the timeout is configurable.
_PromotionLock.__exit__ | low | Unlocks using platform-specific primitives; if _fh is None, returns False. | Verify that __exit__ is always called after __enter__ succeeds.
